title: Crews and coordinated outages

blocks.text: A rural electric cooperative is scheduling its feeder upgrades year by year, and the model in `outages.py` already has a start variable `x[(pid, year)]` for each project and each year in its window, a row saying each project starts at most once, and a row saying each must-do project starts exactly once. Two rules from the operations team are missing:

items: **Crews.** Each year only a few line crews can be mobilized: at most `max_starts[year]` projects may start in that year, must-do projects included. A year in which no project may start has nothing to cap, so it gets no row. In Python an empty `sum` is the number 0, and MathOpt refuses a row built from it (a `TypeError` about a `bool`): skip the row, or start the sum from `mathopt.LinearExpression()`, as the lesson shows.

**Coordinated outages.** Some pairs of upgrades sit on the same feeder and need one shared outage. For each pair in `coordinated`, either neither project is funded, or both are and they start in the same year.

blocks.text: Write `add_outage_rules(model, x, projects, max_starts, coordinated)` so the model allows exactly the schedules that keep both rules.

The model so far, with $`P`$ the projects, $`T_i`$ the years project $`i`$ may start in, $`M \subseteq P`$ the must-do projects, $`Y`$ the years with a crew cap $`K_y`$, and $`D`$ the coordinated pairs:
Write your rows in this notation first, each with its quantifier and a label, then code them. Mind the pairs whose windows do not line up: there is no variable for a year outside a project's window.
The tests fix a schedule by setting the variables' bounds and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct formulation passes. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a schedule within every year's crew cap is allowed, and one that starts too many projects in a year is refused
a coordinated pair started together is allowed, and one member funded alone is refused
a coordinated pair funded in two different years is refused
a coordinated pair whose windows share no year may not have either member funded
a year that starts fewer projects than its crew cap is allowed
a must-do project uses one of its start year's crews

origin.section: A Timing Window Is Enforced by the Variables You Never Create

concepts: one binary per project and allowed start year makes every start-dependent quantity linear
a timing window is enforced by creating start variables only for the window's years
